bug_semantics: When OAuth2 is enabled, the unauthenticated /oauth/login handler creates a state value and writes it into the handler-wide registeredStates Go map. net/http runs requests concurrently, but the map's writes and the callback/authentication reads and writes had no mutex. Parallel login requests can therefore produce Go's fatal concurrent map writes panic and terminate OliveTin remotely; callback and cookie-auth traffic supplies additional read/write race paths.
flaw_origin: Commit 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734 introduced OAuth2 in internal/httpservers/oauth2.go as a new file, including the shared registeredStates map, the unlocked registeredStates[state] assignment in handleOAuthLogin, unlocked state lookups, and public /oauth/login and /oauth/callback route registration in internal/httpservers/singleFrontend.go. Its direct parent has neither the OAuth2 source file nor any registeredStates symbol. Later commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 moved the same state map into OAuth2Handler, and be7c75404377ccddd07e16b57e39ead5609323f7 renamed/moved the file, but both preserved the already-vulnerable unsynchronized mechanism and are not introducers.
ai_marker: absent: the exact raw BIC commit object has author 'jamesread <contact@jread.com>', committer 'James Read <contact@jread.com>', subject 'feature: OAuth2! :-D', no message body or trailers, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with marker, and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party repository advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-45m3-398w-m2m9 identifies service/internal/auth/otoauth2/restapi_auth_oauth2.go registeredStates, unlocked write at line 141, unlocked read at 174, callback writes at 284-285, auth-chain read at 376, and public routes at service/internal/httpservers/frontend.go lines 71-72. It reports the unauthenticated concurrent /oauth/login crash and links the direct fix https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36.

At 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734, git show proves internal/httpservers/oauth2.go was added from /dev/null with package-global registeredStates = make(map[string]*oauth2State), handleOAuthLogin's unlocked registeredStates[state] write, callback/cookie reads, and internal/httpservers/singleFrontend.go's /oauth/login and /oauth/callback registrations. git log -L 105,123:internal/httpservers/oauth2.go at the candidate resolves the vulnerable handler block directly to this new-file commit, and git log --reverse -S'registeredStates[state]' -- internal/httpservers/oauth2.go returns this commit as the first occurrence.

Direct-parent verification: 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734 has sole parent b31cdf15a20c29f6301f02a3ba4ef97b9d99e48c. git ls-tree -r --name-only on that parent returns no internal/httpservers/oauth2.go or oauth2_providers.go, and git grep -n registeredStates b31cdf15a20c29f6301f02a3ba4ef97b9d99e48c -- '*.go' returns no match. Thus the vulnerable lines and mechanism are absent from the immediate parent tree.

The candidate is a one-parent, standalone feature commit rather than a merge, move, revert, or identifiable squash aggregate. Subsequent history/blame follows the same mechanism through a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 (state moved into OAuth2Handler) and be7c75404377ccddd07e16b57e39ead5609323f7 (R090 move to service/internal/auth/otoauth2/restapi_auth_oauth2.go), so no later preservation commit displaces the smaller original BIC.

Fix-parent proof: f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36 has sole parent aa2bd95ccb8f00a1c97ebcb0a03e8d49867ffde6. git grep on that parent shows the map at service/internal/auth/otoauth2/restapi_auth_oauth2.go:24, unlocked login write at 147, callback read at 180, callback writes at 290-291, and cookie-auth read at 382, with no sync.RWMutex. The f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36 diff adds sync.RWMutex and brackets every listed map access with Lock/RLock and matching unlocks, including a locked lookupOAuth2UserByState helper. This directly removes the advisory's concurrent-map panic mechanism.

Version cross-check: tags 3000.10.0 (d22bdebff7c7fd54508d12758d5f8cf3f8bf7ac3), 3000.10.1 (60176b6078ed32aa664329c50aa5a42604dc3f96), and 3000.10.2 (2eb5f0ba79d4bbef3c802bf8b4666a7e18dcfd90) all contain the BIC and show registeredStates accesses without sync.RWMutex; none contains f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36. Tag 3000.11.0 (235493e471249b07cf20abdf5850f9ba38d8effa) contains f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36 and shows the RWMutex plus locked accesses. The bundle's first-patched Go pseudo-version 0.0.0-20260301235225-f044d90d5525c resolves exactly to the fix commit. The repository advisory currently labels <=3000.10.0 affected and 3000.10.3 patched even though its own description says 3000.10.1 has the pattern; the validated clone and git ls-remote have no 3000.10.3 tag, while source inspection proves 3000.10.1 and 3000.10.2 vulnerable and 3000.11.0 fixed.

There is no commit-object AI marker or bot identity. No PR text, later commit, or fix attribution is used for this decision.
reasoning: The advisory's failure is caused by concurrent access to one shared ordinary Go map, not merely by the later file layout. The first commit that makes the crash reachable is 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734: it creates the map, performs an unlocked write for every public OAuth2 login request, supplies unlocked reads, and registers the unauthenticated routes. The direct parent lacks the files and symbol, while -L and -S history identify the same first-writing commit; later handler encapsulation and path moves only preserve the flaw. The vulnerable mechanism persists through the 3000.10.x tags available in repository history. Direct fix f044d90d5525c4c8e3f421b32ed7eff771c22d36 adds the missing synchronization on all advisory-listed accesses, is the exact pseudo-version boundary in the bundle, and is present in fixed tag 3000.11.0. Finally, the raw BIC commit object has a human author and committer and no AI-related trailer, disclosure, or bot identity. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the causal verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
